final_recommendation: The room converged on a labor-only Protocol amendment with a tripartite enforcement panel (Mexico-led inspectors, independent review, automatic fines after appeals), explicitly carving out dairy and Chapter 19 to secure Canadian support. Labor and business committed to coordinated public endorsement contingent on Pelosi scheduling a floor vote by end-of-week, creating maximum pressure for ratification before recess.
minority_objections: Mexico initially resisted automatic fines as potential sovereignty infringement until 'presumption of inspector competence' language was secured
Canada threatened withdrawal if amendment scope expanded beyond labor-only provisions
key_conflicts: Labor enforcement adequacy vs. Mexico's sovereignty concerns over U.S.-controlled inspection/penalty mechanisms
Business demand for certainty vs. labor demand for binding enforcement teeth
Timeline pressure (vote before recess) vs. need for airtight charter language satisfying all parties
key_concessions: Mexico accepted tripartite panel with automatic fines in exchange for 'presumption of inspector competence' and factual-appeal-only framework
Labor accepted Mexico-led inspectors (not U.S. inspectors) in exchange for independent review panel and mandatory penalties
U.S. Democrats committed to labor-only scope, explicitly protecting Canada's dairy and Chapter 19 settlements
red_lines: Canada: any reopening of dairy or Chapter 19 provisions kills ratification
Labor: no floor vote without binding enforcement mechanism (not just text commitments)
Mexico: no 'receivership' model where Washington unilaterally decides enforcement
Business: no indefinite delay—vote must occur before recess or coalition fractures
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Pelosi's actual willingness/ability to schedule floor vote by Friday remained unconfirmed—room assumed pressure would force movement
Risk that public ultimatum strategy backfires if Pelosi doesn't move, flipping narrative to 'Democrats killed the deal'
Enforceability of 'labor-only' scope in future political contexts—no mechanism discussed to prevent future attempts to leverage labor amendment for other concessions
downstream_risk_variables: Pelosi's floor scheduling decision by Friday determines whether coalition holds or fractures
Media narrative pivot point: 'enforcement is real' vs. 'Congress stalling' depends entirely on vote commitment
Mexico's domestic ratification contingent on seeing actual U.S. congressional action, not just coalition statements
January 2020 reopening risk if vote doesn't occur before recess—Democrats may demand stronger enforcement language in writing
uncertainty_notes: The room achieved consensus on charter language and coalition strategy but left Pelosi's floor scheduling decision—the critical variable for ratification success—entirely unresolved. All parties acknowledged the Friday deadline as make-or-break but had no confirmed read on leadership's actual intent. The coordinated public pressure strategy is high-risk: it either forces immediate movement or exposes the coalition to narrative collapse if the vote doesn't materialize.

marker_evidence.ratification_risk: Dominated every round—'doesn't get a floor vote' (R1), 'deal dies in 2020' (R2-R5), coalition's entire strategy built around unlocking ratification via amendment
marker_evidence.labor_enforcement_pressure: Central driver throughout—'unions won't move without it' (R1), automatic fines/inspections demanded (R1-R3), AFL-CIO endorsement contingent on binding mechanism (R4)
marker_evidence.business_lobby_support: Genuine consideration but not dominant—Roundtable mobilization conditional on tripartite panel (R2), timeline pressure applied (R4-R5), but reactive to labor/congressional demands rather than driving
marker_evidence.canadian_domestic_acceptability: Repeatedly surfaced as veto threat—'Canada's not reopening' (R1), explicit carve-out demanded (R3-R4), but resolved early via charter language rather than driving ongoing discussion
marker_evidence.mexico_labor_sovereignty_risk: Serious consideration but resolved—'receivership' concern (R1-R2), 'presumption of inspector competence' negotiated (R3), satisfied by R4 ('charter locks our sovereignty')
marker_evidence.media_public_pressure: Genuine tactical consideration—'story flips' narrative (R3), 'Now it's on Pelosi' framing (R5), but used instrumentally to pressure Pelosi rather than driving substantive terms
marker_evidence.agreement_stability: Core premise throughout—entire room operated on assumption that original package couldn't pass as-is, amendment necessary for ratification ('conditional votes' R1, 'deal dies' if no amendment R2-R5)
